newsitem.title: USA: Upward pressure seen on US labor costs--Dallas Fed.
newsitem.headline: Upward pressure seen on US labor costs--Dallas Fed.

text.p: Dallas Federal Reserve Bank President Robert McTeer said U.S. wages were rising and perhaps at a slightly faster pace than national productivity.
Such a phenomenon, he noted, adds some upward pressure to unit labor costs.

"Wages are rising and they may be rising a little faster than productivity right now," McTeer told an audience at Midwestern State University here. "So, there is some upward pressure on unit labor costs."
The Dallas Fed president said the state of the economy is "excellent," adding that recent economic data show strength across the board.
"For over a month now, just about every economic report has been stronger than expected; there have been practically no weak reports," McTeer said.

The Federal Reserve raised short-term interest rates by 25 basis points at its Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25, bringing the overnight bank lending, or federal funds, rate to 5.50 percent.
At its latest FOMC meeting, the central bank said it was raising interest rates in "a prudent step" to prolong the seven-year old U.S. economic expansion.
McTeer is a member of the FOMC. He is not scheduled to vote on policy actions in 1997 due to the committee's internal rotation rules.
